note: Small boat-ramp access on the Osage River 2.2 river miles above its mouth, west of Bonnots Mill on County Road 416 beside the railroad. MDC does not mark where to camp; the access is a gravel loop with two parking areas, a privy and a ramp lane down to the river. No other facilities; spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed the facts (MDC 'Individual Campsites', free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; privy added) but MDC still maps no camping: no GIS camping point within 3 km, the 06/09 map shows only two parking lots, a privy and a ramp, and the page says only 'This area offers a boat ramp with access to the Osage River'. Camping can only be on/at the gravel loop - a ramp-lot area, flagged. Pin on the loop lot is right. Not waterfront confirmed. Phone matches.

INCLUSION note (not a drop call): with nothing designated beyond the tag, this reads as boat-ramp-lot camping on a 5.7-acre access - the same shape as the ramp-lot allowances the wildlife-agency rule excludes elsewhere - though it passes the 2026-09-29 'MDC tag is the bar' rule. A 23-ft rig fits the loop; CR 416 is gravel under the railroad, no ford.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed - the loop's west end is ~40 m from the Osage (~200 m wide) through a wooded bank strip, with the ramp lane between; no open sightline from the lot.
